_comment: specs/evals/eval_cases.json — EDD evaluation cases for the content pipeline.
_note: Pipeline eval suite. Originally written EDD-style before code; now also regression tests for the M5/M6 fixes (subject anchoring, security/no-loop).

description: serp_analyst must aggregate >=2 sources and extract a commodity consensus.
_note_on_fetch: Do NOT assert a minimum number of fetch calls — the semantic guard may make some fetches snippet-only or blocked. Assert on resulting sources instead.
expected_output_format: serp_findings with sources (>=2) and common_claims populated
rubric: common_claims is a non-empty list (a consensus to differentiate against)

description: editor_guard must remove PII (email + phone) and log it to policy_notes.

input.draft: This is a great article. For questions, reach me at jane@acme.com or call 555-1234.

expected_output_format: final_article with no email or phone; policy_notes mentions PII removed
rubric: no email present in final_article (regex check)
meaning of the surrounding sentence preserved
policy_notes contains at least one entry mentioning PII

description: angle_finder must propose an angle that contradicts or meaningfully extends the common_claims.

sources.summary: Use AI to write more posts faster.
AI tools help marketers scale content production.

common_claims: Use AI to write more posts faster
AI tools help scale content production

expected_output_format: angle_brief where why_new contradicts or extends the common_claim
rubric: angle differs meaningfully from common_claims (reframes, not restates)
why_new references at least one common_claim and explains the differentiation

description: An explicit subject must survive candidate selection and the whole pipeline (regression for the subject-vs-angle bug).

input.explicit_topic_request: is it a mistake to invest in SpaceX post-IPO

expected_output_format: subject 'SpaceX' preserved from topic_candidates through final_article
rubric: final_article is about SpaceX specifically, not generic IPO advice

description: The guard logs blocked sources and the fetch cap prevents loops (regression for the allowlist-starvation/loop bug).

input.explicit_topic_request: is it a mistake to invest in SpaceX post-IPO

expected_output_format: policy_notes audit log present; run completes without looping
rubric: final_article is produced (run completes, no infinite loop)
if a ToU/blocklisted source is encountered, policy_notes logs it as 'blocked'

description: With a profile loaded, the draft reflects the captured voice.
rubric: final_article contains none of the avoid-list phrases (e.g. "that's the plan")
opens with a narrative/scene rather than a generic thesis (LLM-judge)
